knownLimits: An env var holding true/false resolves to a bool, and the (string) cast gives '1' or '' (URL '1', token '1'; URL '', token null). Craft's own App::parseEnv() returns the bool, so this is the cast, not Craft.
A key or URL of '0', literal or from an env var, gives token null. The old '$s->apiKey ?: null' did the same, so nothing changed.

A literal API key shaped like '$word' (only \w characters after the $) is now read as an env var name: unset gives no token. Same for a value starting with a defined @alias. This is Craft's convention.

An unset or empty env var for daemonUrl/apiUrl gives url '', and Guzzle throws 'URI must include a scheme and host' at request time. The old literal '$NAME' threw the same message, so nothing became less clear.
Craft 4.5 parseEnv was not read from source (only 5.11.3 is installed locally); composer.json allows ^4.5.
